issues.legal_issue: A landlord may waive a statutory exemption enacted for the landlord’s private benefit, and an agreement doing so is not void where the statute does not prohibit waiver, performance does not require disobedience of law, and no public policy is infringed.
material_facts: A tenant temporarily vacated a shop so the landlord could reconstruct it, under an agreement providing that the tenant would resume possession afterward at the same rent.
The agreement stated that the rent-control protections would apply to the renewed tenancy and that the landlord would not claim the benefit of the exemption for newly constructed buildings.
After reconstruction, the tenant resumed possession and offered rent, which the landlord refused; the landlord then sued to evict the tenant.
The lower courts disagreed about whether the landlord could rely on the exemption and whether the agreement was unlawful.
issues.conclusion: The landlord could waive the exemption, and the agreement was not void under section 23 of the Indian Contract Act. The tenant was entitled to the protection of the rent-control law, and the trial court’s decision was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 1-A of the U.P. (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, exempted qualifying newly constructed buildings from the Act, while section 3 restricted eviction of protected tenants. An advantage conferred solely for a person’s private benefit may generally be waived if there is no statutory prohibition and waiver does not infringe public rights or public policy. Under section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an agreement is unlawful if its performance necessarily entails transgression of law; an agreement to waive an exemption is not unlawful merely because the exemption exists. The Court approved Neminath Appayya Hanumannavar v. Jamboorao Satappa Kocheri, AIR 1966 Mys. 154, and referred to Vita Food Products Incorporated v. Unus Company Ltd. (in Liquidation), [1939] AC 277.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_dispute and post_cutoff_construction and express_agreement_to_apply_protection and exemption_is_private_benefit and no_anti_waiver_bar and performance_needs_no_lawbreaking and no_public_policy_conflict

predicates.tenant_eviction_dispute: A landlord brought an eviction dispute against a tenant occupying the premises.
predicates.post_cutoff_construction: The premises were constructed or reconstructed after the point at which the statutory exemption applied.
predicates.express_agreement_to_apply_protection: The landlord and tenant agreed that the tenant-protection rules would apply and that the landlord would not claim the exemption.
predicates.exemption_is_private_benefit: The exemption provided an advantage for the private benefit of the property owner.
predicates.no_anti_waiver_bar: The statutory rule contained no prohibition against the owner agreeing not to claim the exemption.
predicates.performance_needs_no_lawbreaking: Carrying out the agreement did not necessarily require either party to disobey the law.
predicates.no_public_policy_conflict: The agreement did not infringe a public right or conflict with public policy.

issues.definition: When an eviction dispute involves newly constructed premises and the parties expressly agree to apply tenant protections, the agreement is enforceable if the exemption is a private benefit, waiver is not barred, performance requires no lawbreaking, and there is no public-policy conflict.
